{{Short description|Italian computer scientist}}
{{Notability|1=Academics|date=January 2025}}
'''Alessandro Chiesa''' is an Italian computer scientist. He is an associate professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (EPFL), and a now-adjunct professor at [[University of California, Berkeley]]. He has contributed to the field of [[zero-knowledge proofs]], and was a co-founder of [[Zcash]] and [[StarkWare Industries]].<ref name="homepage" />

== Biography ==
Chiesa was born in [[Varese]], Italy in 1987. He studied math and computer science at MIT, where he earned his SB, MEng and PhD. His PhD was in [[theory of computation]], advised by [[Silvio Micali]] at the [[MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory]].<ref name="homepage">{{Cite web |title=Alessandro Chiesa |url=https://ic-people.epfl.ch/~achiesa/}}</ref>

Chiesa became an assistant professor at UC Berkeley in 2015. In 2018 he was named in MIT's [[Innovators Under 35]] list.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alessandro Chiesa |url=https://people.epfl.ch/alessandro.chiesa?lang=en}}</ref> In 2021 he became an associate professor at EPFL.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CS Faculty List |url=https://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Faculty/Lists/CS/faculty.html}}</ref>

== Research ==
In 2013, Chiesa coauthored a paper and implementation of TinyRAM, a virtual machine whose execution could be proven using zero-knowledge proofs.<ref>{{Cite conference |title=SNARKs for C: Verifying Program Executions Succinctly and in Zero Knowledge |conference=CRYPTO 2013 |last1=Ben-Sasson |first1=Eli |last2=Chiesa |first2=Alessandro |last3=Genkin |first3=Daniel |last4=Tromer |first4=Eran |last5=Virza |first5=Madars}}</ref>

In 2014, Chiesa coauthored the design of Zerocash,<ref>{{Cite conference |title=Zerocash: Decentralized Anonymous Payments from Bitcoin |last1=Ben-Sasson | first1=Eli |last2=Chiesa |first2=Alessandro |last3=Garman |first3=Christina |last4=Green |first4=Matthew |last5=Miers |first5=Ian |last6=Eran |first6=Tromer |last7=Virza |first7=Madars |conference=2014 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy}}</ref> which laid the foundation for the [[Zcash]] protocol. The work was recognized by the Test of Time Award at the [[IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy]].<ref name="test of time">{{Cite web |title=45th IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy |url=https://sp2024.ieee-security.org/awards.html}}</ref>

In 2020, Chiesa coauthored the design of Zexe, a related protocol which drew on ideas from Zerocash and extended it to arbitrary computations.<ref>{{Cite conference |title=Zexe: Enabling decentralized private computation |last1=Bowe |first1=Sean |last2=Chiesa |first2=Alessandro |last3=Green |first3=Matthew |last4=Miers |first4=Ian |last5=Mishra |first5=Pratyush |last6=Wu |first6=Howard |conference=2020 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)}}</ref> The Zexe design became the foundation of a blockchain called Aleo.<ref>{{Cite conference |title=SoK: Privacy-Preserving Computing in the Blockchain Era |last1=Almashaqbeh |first1=Ghada |last2=Solomon |first2=Ravital |conference=2022 IEEE 7th European Symposium on Security and Privacy}}</ref>

* Okawa Foundation Research Grant (2020)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alessandro Chiesa receives 2020 Okawa Research Grant |url=https://eecs.berkeley.edu/news/alessandro-chiesa-receives-2020-okawa-research-grant/}}</ref>
* [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] (2021)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alessandro Chiesa named 2021 Sloan Research Fellow |url=https://eecs.berkeley.edu/news/alessandro-chiesa-named-2021-sloan-research-fellow/}}</ref>
* [[IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy]] Test-of-Time Award (2024)<ref name="test of time" />
